recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-16365 unless a future issue identifies a current active medication-definition example with the same type/category defect.
issue_request: FHIR-16365 was a Published FHIR-core BR&R change request with resolution Persuasive. It reported that the MedicinalProductPharmaceutical example was actually an AdverseEvent resource and was categorized as Clinical.Summary; Jira comments recorded agreement with the defect and planned R5 medication-definition improvements.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-16365. Git history shows the relevant example defect was corrected implicitly by commit 1872be78f8348709a4c36f062ec3f156814ca011, which changed the old medicinalproductpharmaceutical-example.xml root from AdverseEvent to MedicinalProductPharmaceutical in July 2018. The same family was later covered by FHIR-17364, whose Jira resolution says the fix had already been done.
additional_context: MedicinalProductPharmaceutical is outside the current build. Current source/fhir.ini activates AdministrableProductDefinition as the replacement medication-definition resource and maps MedicinalProductPharmaceutical to AdministrableProductDefinition for version-change handling. Commit e45413f7a7 removed the old MedicinalProductPharmaceutical source files during R4B/R5 medication-definition work. FHIR-17364, the broader MedicinalProduct* invalid-example issue, is already represented on the combined branch by commit 6d7867c3f4857e8c7dd1a75df242a59d81c132f1.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active replacement example is an AdministrableProductDefinition resource, its StructureDefinition category is Specialized.Medication Definition, and scans found no AdverseEvent or Clinical.Summary residue in the active administrable-product source.
